skill.name: linejig
skill.description: Create interactive Three.js illustrations of a single object from simple geometric shapes. Add an assembly or draw-on animation and give one focal part a hover and click response.
skill.summary: Build and embed interactive 3D line illustrations with a consistent visual style.
skill.author: 37degree-studio

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown syntax, drawing terms, or loopback testing rather than shell execution, reconnaissance, or path traversal. The starter loads unverified remote assets, and the guides leave gaps in iframe action validation and deployment authorization. No evidence found of prompt injection or data exfiltration in the bundled files.

remediation.issue: The starter loads remote runtime assets without verifying their integrity.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle reviewed, pinned copies of the kernel, styles, and Three.js dependencies. Verify checksums before updating the bundled assets.

remediation.issue: The gallery workflow does not distinguish design approval from authorization to deploy.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit permission to publish before pushing gallery changes or redeploying. Confirm the repository, branch, and deployment environment.

remediation.issue: The example forwards iframe action IDs without validating the message payload.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the origin and source checks. Validate the message shape, expected figure identity, and allowed action IDs before calling a host handler.

semantic_findings.description: In the Linejig source repository, the workflow treats words like "final" as approval to push and redeploy. Design approval does not necessarily authorize a public release.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly connects illustration approval to push and redeploy steps. It does not require separate permission to publish.

content.value_statement: Static illustrations cannot show how a part moves or responds to a visitor. Linejig helps you build a Three.js figure with a clear silhouette, a short intro, and one focal interaction.
actual_capabilities: Propose three single-object concepts and recommend one based on the surrounding content.
Build a 2:1 axonometric figure from rounded solids with consistent on-screen line widths.
Apply line art, Brand, Dots, Readout, or Pencil styling to the same model.
Animate an ordered assembly or draw-on intro and add hover and click behavior to a focal part.
Embed a figure in a page and coordinate its theme and action events with the host.
Guide browser checks for frozen animation frames, desktop and phone layouts, and reduced motion.
limitations: Each figure centers on one object and one interactive part or family of matching parts.
Existing SVGs are visual references and must be rebuilt by hand. The kernel does not import or trace them.
The bundled starter loads its kernel from Linejig and Three.js from a CDN. Offline use requires local copies.
Line art does not include captions, labels, or logos. Brand style allows short part labels, not calls to action.

use_cases.title: Design an Empty State
use_cases.description: Create a letter tray whose flap opens when clicked to reinforce the empty inbox message.

use_cases.title: Embed a Themed Figure
use_cases.description: Match an embedded illustration to an app's light and dark surfaces and connect an approved action to the host interface.

use_cases.title: Illustrate Mechanical Assembly
use_cases.description: Show how a desktop compass fits together by animating the base, support, and needle in assembly order.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Object
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: plan an illustration before writing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose three objects for an empty reading list. Name one moving part and its click response for each concept. Recommend one and wait for my choice.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Line Art Figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an axonometric desk compass in line art. Draw the compass in from left to right and let the needle follow the pointer. Include a still state for reduced motion.

prompt_templates.title: Restyle and Verify a Figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: use a confirmed brand color without changing the model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Restyle my existing figure in Brand using the approved color #2f6bff. Keep its model and motion. Check that the focal part stays readable on light and dark surfaces at phone width.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a Figure Action
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect an illustration to a host interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Embed the inbox figure in our React app with matching light and dark surfaces. Only the expected frame and compose action should open the composer. Add an equivalent accessible button.

output_examples.input: Create a camera illustration for a photo import screen.
output_examples.output: A compact camera assembles from the body outward. The shutter button focuses the lens on hover and triggers a shutter animation on click.

output_examples.input: Show a letter tray for an empty inbox and give readers a way to compose a message.
output_examples.output: A letter tray appears on a surface that matches the host theme. Clicking the figure or using the separate Compose button opens the composer.

output_examples.input: Check the compass at phone width with reduced motion enabled.
output_examples.output: The compass opens in its final pose. The full needle stays inside the frame at phone width, and the page does not scroll horizontally.

best_practices: Choose an object that is recognizable at thumbnail size without a caption.
Fit the frame to the widest pose and make parts move in the order they would on the real object.
Check the intro and final state on desktop and phone in both themes. Verify that reduced motion skips the intro.
anti_patterns: Do not add multiple unrelated objects or independent interactions to one illustration.
Do not add dense surface detail, logos, or instructional labels to line art.
Do not make clicking the figure the only way to perform a host action.

faq.question: Which visual styles are available?
faq.answer: Line art is the default. The same model can also use Brand, Dots, Readout, or Pencil.

faq.question: Can I use my own brand color?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply a confirmed hex color for Brand, Dots, Readout, or Pencil. The default line art stays grayscale.

faq.question: Can I import an existing SVG directly?
faq.answer: No. Use your SVG as a reference and rebuild its main shapes with the kernel's geometry.

faq.question: Which intro animations are supported?
faq.answer: The figure can assemble in layers or draw its lines on screen. You can also show the finished figure without playing an intro.

faq.question: Does the figure respect reduced motion?
faq.answer: Yes. The kernel can show the finished pose without playing the intro.

faq.question: Can I host a figure in my own app?
faq.answer: Yes. Serve a figure page from your app or embed a published gallery figure in an iframe. The starter uses remote dependencies unless you replace them.
